http://www.parisguardian.com/news/279209.text: 'Standing shoulder to shoulder': Macron pledges national recovery as unprecedented wildfires ravage France and Spain ANI 26 Jul 2026, 02:27 GMT+10 Paris [France], July 26 (ANI): Pledging that the nation will overcome its ongoing crisis, French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday (local time) praised the resilience of emergency crews and citizens as 'a united people, standing shoulder to shoulder' against raging wildfires. Macron, in a post on X, confirmed full civil and military deployment, including water-bomber planes and military transport aircraft. 'In these hours when the flames are severely testing our country, France reveals what it is: a united people, standing shoulder to shoulder. Thank you to our firefighters, our military personnel, the civil security forces, our gendarmes and police officers, as well as to the farmers and entrepreneurs, who through their commitment and courage, relentlessly combat the fires,' Macron stated, noting that 'All civil and military resources are mobilized: civil security aerial resources, Canadair, Dash, water-bomber helicopters, reinforcements from across France. One first illustrates the adaptability of our armed forces: the A400M is engaged in support of operations.' The fires have heavily impacted Gironde, Landes, Occitanie, Var, Hautes-Alpes, and Haute-Corse. Acknowledging the scale of destruction, Macron noted that 'thousands of hectares have been ravaged, homes destroyed, activities disrupted, lives upended'. However, the President assured affected residents, displaced families, local mayors, and prefects of the government's unwavering commitment and said, 'We will rebuild, we will repair, and we will be there as long as it takes.' The French President further thanked Romania, Croatia, Germany, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia for dispatching critical emergency aid. 'This is Europe,' Macron declared. 'In times of trial, it brings to life the solidarity that defines it'. He also extended solidarity to neighbouring countries enduring similar conditions, adding that France's 'thoughts also go to Spain, Italy, Greece, and all the peoples who are also facing wildfires'. https://x.com/EmmanuelMacron/status/2081058742280303075 Meanwhile, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, describing the crisis as a 'historic situation' requiring a 'historic mobilisation,' announced that nearly 100,000 hectares have burned across the national territory. With around thirty fires simultaneously active, more than 167,000 people have been evacuated to ensure their safety. The situation remains particularly critical in Gironde, where sudden weather shifts have altered the fire's dynamics. 'After a slight improvement last night and this morning, the forecasts are once again becoming unfavourable,' Nunez warned. 'The coming hours could be difficult.' Following a second interministerial crisis meeting within 24 hours, additional reinforcements have also been dispatched to Landes, Var, Corsica, and Hautes-Alpes. 'The ground resources of the firefighters have been massively redeployed to the Southwest in order to concentrate our efforts where the situation is most critical. 1,400 firefighters, 1,500 military personnel, and 1,700 internal security forces are now engaged in fighting the fires, protecting populations, and securing evacuated areas,' he wrote in a post on X. He noted that the healthcare network is actively managing the human toll, distributing 2.5 million FFP2 masks to protect against smoke, deploying 20 military ambulances, and delivering 3,500 camp beds to reception centres. The Minister added that on Monday, government officials will meet with tourism and energy leaders to plan recovery efforts. https://x.com/SebLecornu/status/2081075555202384013 The remarks come as unprecedented wildfires sweeping through western France and central Spain have forced more than 250,000 residents and tourists to flee, as raging flames destroy vast forest tracts and residential communities near Bordeaux and Madrid. According to Deutsche Welle (DW), emergency responders face blazes of historic proportions, the largest recorded in both nations in recent years, which firefighters admit are too massive to tackle head-on. Along France's Atlantic coast, approximately 44,000 people were evacuated from the Cap Ferret peninsula, with many transported to safety by boat. Near Bordeaux, the renowned wine-producing hub, entire towns were emptied 'as a precaution' as gale-force winds pushed advancing flames closer to urban areas. In total, French authorities confirm that over 197,000 people have been evacuated across the western Gironde and Landes departments. Although investigators indicate the two primary French blazes were ignited accidentally, environmental authorities emphasise that increasingly hotter and drier summer conditions have exponentially magnified the severity of such outbreaks, DW reported. The human toll across Southern Europe continues to rise. Dozens of firefighters have been injured, and three have lost their lives this week--two near Bordeaux, France, and one in Sicily, Italy, where major wildfires are also burning. On the other hand, in Spain, the Interior Ministry reported that 70,000 people have fled their homes. Spanish officials confirmed a wildfire fatality in Manises, near Valencia, where local emergency teams brought the blaze under control but noted that 'unfortunately the fire has claimed the life of one person' after the victim's body was discovered in a vehicle within a ravine, DW reported. Spain has officially declared a national emergency as two separate blazes near Madrid merged into a single massive front. Emergency management services for the Madrid region warned that the combined inferno has reached 'its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain.' Meanwhile, in Guadalajara province, the largest active fire in the region has scorched roughly 32,000 hectares. Inspecting affected zones west of Madrid as local temperatures surpassed 37C (98.6F), Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez reaffirmed that the top priority remains 'to save lives.' In an official address shared on X, Prime Minister Sanchez stated, 'Our priority is safeguarding lives, defending population centres, and combating the flames. The entire State, all Administrations, are coordinating all resources for an effective response to the fires and for the reception of evacuated and confined people. Today we are in the fight and in the extinguishing, but the Government of Spain will also be in the reconstruction and recovery of the affected areas.' DW reported that in order to assist both countries, the European Commission announced the dispatch of specialised firefighting aircraft, sending three planes to France and four to Spain to support containment operations. More on this topic Welcome back to World Brief, where we’re looking at missile incursions into NATO airspace, a potential new front in the Iran war , and the likely winner of Greater Manchester ’s mayoral race. ‘Another Reckless Act’ Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened an emergency meeting on Thursday to address an overnight missile incursion believed to be of Russian origin. Welcome back to World Brief, where we’re looking at missile incursions into NATO airspace, a potential new front in the Iran war , and the likely winner of Greater Manchester ’s mayoral race. ‘Another Reckless Act’ Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened an emergency meeting on Thursday to address an overnight missile incursion believed to be of Russian origin. Although Tusk stopped short of directly blaming Moscow, experts said that the projectile appears to be a Russian Kh-101 missile that was launched into eastern Poland during Russia’s overnight strikes on Ukraine. “There was no direct threat because the missile ​landed in an uninhabited area,” Tusk said on Thursday, adding that “we were ready to shoot it down had it continued its flight.” NATO jets had scrambled to intercept the missile before it crashed. Still, the incident has once again raised European concerns about the war spilling over into NATO countries, particularly as Russia intensifies its assault; Moscow’s overnight operation saw dozens of missiles and hundreds of drones primarily target the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv as well as the western city of Lviv, which sits on the border with Poland. At least nine people were killed, including at least three children, and more than 50 others were wounded. Tusk suggested on Thursday that Poland was likely not purposefully targeted. However, NATO chief Mark Rutte warned that even accidents carry grave risks. “This incident is yet another reckless act by Russia and a dangerous consequence of its war against Ukraine,” Rutte wrote on ​X. He condemned Moscow’s overnight strikes and vowed to continue NATO support for Kyiv’s war effort. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha similarly blamed Russia for threatening a wider regional war with its incursion into Poland. “This is yet another clear demonstration that strengthening Ukraine’s air defense now is urgent and serves as a guarantee for the protection of the entire Euro-Atlantic community,” Sybiha wrote on X. Over the past year, NATO members have accused both Russian and Ukrainian forces of launching stray drones, missiles, and aircraft into the airspaces of Denmark, Estonia, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, and Romania, among others. Last September, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed creating a drone wall to counter such incursions, and in December, Poland unveiled plans to complete a roughly $2.3 billion anti-drone fortification system. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky used Russia’s overnight assault and alleged incursion into Poland to call for more military aid. “All partners know how and with what they can help,” Zelensky wrote on X on Thursday. “Untimely assistance and delays in the delivery of anti-ballistic missiles lead to this ​kind of destruction, these kinds of casualties that, unfortunately, we are seeing today.” Zelensky told Axios on Tuesday that he had asked U.S. President Donald Trump for an emergency “winter package” of Patriot air defense interceptors during their White House meeting that day. Ukraine’s stockpiles are almost depleted , and only U.S. Patriots have the ability to consistently intercept Russian ballistic missiles. During this month’s NATO leaders’ summit, Trump agreed to give Kyiv a license to produce Patriot missiles for itself; however, he ruled out the delivery of more Patriots during the time that it takes Ukraine to begin manufacturing them. Fighting in the Middle East threatened new fronts on Thursday, after Egypt confirmed that an unidentified drone had struck its Mediterranean port of Damietta the day before. According to Egyptian authorities, the drone hit a U.S.-owned vessel carrying liquified natural gas, sparking a fire that spread onto a second ship. No injuries were reported, and no side has taken responsibility for the attack, though Trump implied on Wednesday that Tehran was responsible. The incident marks the first assault on Egypt since the Iran war began in February, and it comes as both Washington and Tehran are intensifying their operations. According to U.S. Central Command , U.S. forces launched another wave of strikes on dozens of Iranian targets linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps late Wednesday—just hours after the United States carried out joint attacks with Saudi Arabia on Iran-backed militias in Iraq. The Pakistani Foreign Ministry stressed on Thursday that peace talks are still being considered, with Islamabad working to bring both Washington and Tehran to the table. “Negotiations between parties are ongoing, particularly on [the] Strait of Hormuz and to de-escalate,” ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said. An almost guaranteed win. The United Kingdom kicked off its biggest by-election in history on Thursday with a mayoral race for Greater Manchester. Whoever is elected will fill the shoes of Andy Burnham , whose popular tenure running in the northern city helped propel his career to Downing Street—or now, “ No. 10 North .” Labour Party candidate Bev Craig is expected to sweep the vote, with recent polling showing her with a 20-percentage-point lead over rival Sian Astley from the far-right Reform UK party. That may be due in part to Burnham’s ambitious first week in office, during which he introduced a slew of new measures aimed at reducing high costs of living and shifting the country’s economic decision-making out of London. Growing Labour popularity would have been unheard of just a few months ago, when the scandal-ridden party suffered a debilitating defeat in local elections. However, Reform UK’s own internal turmoil could also be costing the far right its chance at a Greater Manchester victory. Last month, party leader Nigel Farage was accused of dubious financial arrangements , triggering a parliamentary inquiry. In response, Farage resigned as a member of Parliament representing Clacton to trigger a by-election for his seat, which he planned to compete for again. The party has thus been forced to redirect its focus away from Greater Manchester to ensure that Farage does not lose his former seat to a literal trash can (aka the satirical character Count Binface ) on Aug. 13. Perfect fire conditions. Dangerous wildfires spread farther in Southern Europe on Thursday, with Turkey warning of fires burning near several tourist hot spots along the Mediterranean coast, including in the cities of Fethiye, Antalya, and Ayvalik. Meanwhile, Greece continues to battle deadly blazes on several islands as well as the mainland. Europe is the world’s fastest-warming continent, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service , with experts suggesting that an unusually wet winter followed by an intense summer heat wave have helped create the perfect environmental conditions for fueling wildfires. “We have difficult days ahead of us,” Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said on Thursday. Blazes also continue to endanger locals in Spain and France, where residents have spent the past week fleeing massive wildfires. Although Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez ‌ downgraded the emergency level for a major fire near Madrid on Thursday, he warned that at least 10 others across the country were cause for concern. And in France, recent wildfires have burned a record-setting 91,024 hectares of land . Odds and Ends Singapore authorities fined a French student $465 on Thursday after he pleaded guilty to a public nuisance charge. In March, Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien filmed himself licking a straw from an orange juice vending machine and putting it back. Although the 19-year-old eventually retrieved the straw before another person could use it, prosecutors accused the social media influencer of undermining confidence in public hygiene. “He is truly sorry for having caused all this trouble,” Maximilien’s lawyer said. The lawyer also noted that the student’s parents will ensure that he pays the fine himself. NATO Russia Ukraine Alexandra Sharp is the World Brief writer at Foreign Policy . https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinat.text: Accessibility Links Seven cool European beach towns you’ll want to book for next summer From Belgian beach clubs to Estonia’s secret spa coast, Chris Haslam selects the new summer not-hot-spots on the new northern riviera Cancale in Brittany Getty images Chris Haslam , Chief Travel Writer, The Sunday Times Friday August 21 2026, 5.00am BST , The Times Listen 0:00 / • 11:20 min Share Share this article Email Twitter Facebook Link Save T he blistering summer of 2026 seems to be coming to an end. In the UK the Met Office has dismissed media reports of a sixth heatwave, saying that while the temperatures could be above average into September in the south, the longer-range forecast highlights an unsettled pattern, with wetter-than-average weather likely. It’s cooling down in France too: last week Météo-France announced “ la fin de l’épisode caniculaire ” — the end of the summer heatwave — with more unsettled conditions arriving. In Greece temperatures between 31C and 34C are forecast, with thunderstorm warnings in place across much of the mainland and Crete, with all fire risks dropping to level two out of five. Most commented 1 Search goes on for 18 missing passengers of capsized Cyprus ferry Europe 80 comments In Spain , though, where Alicante hit 42C on Wednesday, the state weather service, Aemet, warns of “a very high probability” that temperatures will remain well above average throughout what’s left of the summer and into autumn. In Turkey MGM, the state meteorological service, warns that temperatures will be between three and six degrees above normal in the coming weeks, with high to extreme wildfire warnings in effect across coastal areas including Canakkale, Balikesir, Izmir, Aydin, Mugla and Antalya. Next summer the Med could be even hotter. According to the World Meteorological Organization, the so-called super El Niño now developing in the Pacific increases the probability of 2027 being another record-breaking year for heat, drought and wildfires, and there’s a possibility that the after-effects could stoke temperatures further in 2028. If so, many of our southern European playgrounds could become too hot for comfort in the summer months, driving tourists — and families especially — to seek more bearable temperatures in the northerly latitudes. Top stories 1 Top five 2027 cruise and tour packages to book with Times Holidays Promoted content Some may worry that would make a holiday born of necessity rather than desire. The truth is that, from the Côte d’Émeraude in Brittany, along the Côte Fleurie — including Deauville and Trouville — and the vast beaches and chalk cliffs of the Côte d’Opale, up through Flanders, along the Dutch coast, past the Frisian Islands and into the Baltic, there are fabulous stretches of European coast that we’ve never truly explored because, well, the weather in the Med was always better. Advertisement That is changing fast, with southern European summers becoming longer, hotter and, in the school holiday months of July and August, increasingly hazardous. The northern alternatives have long-established infrastructure (Ostend was a crowded holiday resort when Torremolinos was still a struggling fishing village), the cultural attractions absent from the Med’s purpose-built resorts and, in high summer, a healthier climate. Top stories 1 Win a country house break worth up to £1,120 at Mallory Court in Warwickshire Competition Here’s my pick of the most fashionable resorts on Europe’s resurgent northern shore, all with a lovely place to stay. All recommendations within this article are informed by expert editorial opinion. If you click on a link in this story we will earn affiliate revenue 1. Cancale, Brittany, France Cancale has a bobo vibe Alamy While Dinard remains the most stylish resort on Brittany’s Côte d’Émeraude — the belle époque guidebook writer Eugène Herpin called it “ La Nice du Nord ” and it stuck — it’s the oyster port of Cancale, on the leeward side of the Presqu’île du Clos-Poulet, that has the most charm. Yes, it attracts all the rich Parisians to their second homes over the spring bank holiday and les grandes vacances , but they’re more the bobo (bourgeois-bohemian) type than the Charles-Henris you will meet in Dinard. The beaches here suit the bobo vibe, from the Cornish-style sands of the Plage du Verger around to the Alt Emporda-like cove at Port-Picain. Stay at the 12-room Château Richeux, the clifftop villa that’s home to Hugo Roellinger’s Michelin-starred restaurant, Le Coquillage. B&B doubles from £270 (maisons-de-bricourt.com). Take the ferry to St Malo 2. Villerville, Normandy, France La Tour is a two-bedroom holiday home in Villerville Alamy “Ah, Tigreville,” those in the know will say when you mention this village de caractère midway between Honfleur and Deauville on the Côte Fleurie. That’s what this half-timbered fishing village was called when Jean Gabin fell off the wagon and got joyously drunk here with Jean-Paul Belmondo in the 1962 film classic Un singe en hiver — and the brick tower on the seafront that you see in the opening shot is where you are staying. The GR223 coastal path runs along wooded cliffs to the southwest called Les Roches Noires and to the northeast lies the wild Plage de Criqueboeuf with views across the mouth of the Seine to Le Havre. That brick tower is La Tour, a 19th-century atelier transformed into a two-bedroom, two-bathroom holiday home with front-row views of La Manche, bookable via Oliver’s Travels. One night’s self-catering for four from £272. Take the ferry to Le Havre Advertisement 11 of the best affordable hotels in France under £170 3. Knokke-Heist, Flanders, Belgium You can reach Knokke-Heist on the world’s longest tram line Alamy Knokke-Heist is 30 stops from Ostend on the Kusttram, the longest tram line in the world, and is the most fashionable of the 15 resorts on Belgium’s 40-mile coast. But how fashionable is that? So much so that locals describe St Tropez as the Knokke-Heiste of the south, and it’s the kind of town where everyone’s looking out for celebrities you will never recognise. July and August see the so-called Le tout Bruxelles crowd arriving at the VIP end of town, Het Zoute, where they waft from private beach clubs — via a lunch of moules de Zélande in Si Versailles (£30; siversailles.be) and the pop-up luxury shops on the prom — to champagne-fuelled nights dancing on the blond beach. Stay at the Hotel Villa Verdi, a boutique property close to the sands and the trendy Albertplein, aka Place m’as-tu-vu? (Did You See Me Square?). B&B doubles from £249. Take the train to Ostend 4. Scheveningen, The Hague, Netherlands Scheveningen is a popular resort town Getty images The Dutch coast has much in common with Norfolk: a vast beach stretching from the Hook of Holland up to Texel featuring a mix of fishing villages including Egmond aan Zee, wild stretches such as Petten aan Zee, and a couple of big resorts, of which Noordwijk is the most glamorous and Scheveningen is the most fun. This is urban Dutch seaside at its finest, built on six miles of sand lined with bars, restaurants, street markets and strandpaviljoens — or beach clubs — offering all the vibes of the Med and beyond. Xiringuito is reminiscent of the Costa de la Luz in Andalusia; Boomerang Beach is Ibiza; Beachclub Indigo is Thailand; and Hart Beach is SoCal. Don’t stay here, though. The Hague, about 25 minutes away on the tram, has more glamorous options and the best of them is Hotel des Indes, the former baronial mansion opposite the MC Escher museum, bookable via easyJet Holidays.. Four nights’ B&B from £519pp, including flights The best things to do in the Netherlands 5. Sylt, Frisian Islands, Germany Sylt is in the Frisian archipelago in the North Sea Getty images The British have Salcombe, the Americans have the Hamptons and the Germans have Sylt, the northernmost of their Frisian Islands. The 28 miles of silver sands on the North Sea side were formerly a rather bracing spot but in recent years Sylt, described by meteorologists as Germany’s front line of climate change, has seen temperatures rise to summer maximums of 27C. That’s making Sylt even more attractive to the types happy to pay £6 million for the must-have thatched holiday homes known as Reetdachhauser . But Sylt can be affordable too: a supremely comfortable strandkorb , or windproof beach chair, costs £14 a day to rent in Sudwaldchen, and the barbecued pork ribs at Sansibar, the island’s most famous beach restaurant, are £22 (sansibar.de). Nine nights’ B&B — five at the Dorint Strandresort & Spa Sylt/Westerland, two in Hamburg, one in Cologne and one in Utrecht — from £2,099pp, including return rail travel from the UK (tailormaderail.com) Advertisement 6. Sopot, Poland Sopot is on the Polish Riviera, facing out to the Baltic Getty images When Croatia became too hot the Czechs started checking out the Polish Riviera and sparked a tourism boom that has seen visitor numbers rise by more than 50 per cent since the sweltering summer of 2022. Poland has 480 miles of coastline, about 250 of which are made of fine Baltic sand, and investors are staking their claims. One recent report showed that two thirds of all hotel developments in Poland in 2024 took place on this coast, and the travel giant Tui has reaffirmed plans to sell packages to the Baltic. Sopot, just north of Gdansk, is the place to start, because this spa resort, founded in 1823, is where the Polish seaside began. Today it has something of the Biarritz about it: a party town that somehow retains its elegance, a place where banging beach clubs, belle époque villas and a 5,000-seat open-air opera in a pine forest all get along fine in the long Pomeranian summer. Base yourself with Regent Holidays at the Sofitel Grand Sopot, in a 1927 building that faces the beach. Seven nights’ B&B from £2,693pp, including flights and transfers 10 of the best places to visit in Poland 7. Saaremaa, Estonia Saaremaa is Estonia’s largest island Getty images It was mud rather than sand that made Saaremaa’s name. High in sulphur and essential minerals, it brought spa culture to Estonia’s largest island in 1840, turning feudal farmland and fisheries into a retreat attracting the tsars, plus Baltic and Scandinavian aristocracy, for mud wraps, salt treatments and networking. Saaremaa’s capital, Kuressaare, now has seven grand spa hotels, effectively giving one spa treatment spot for every ten inhabitants — the highest concentration in Europe — plus dozens more day spas, saunas and private treatment centres. Summer here brings ten hours of sunshine a day, with nearly 19 hours of daylight in mid-June, and highs of 25C. In late summer the shallow waters of the bay reach 22C, four degrees warmer than Cornwall. As for the beaches, they’re sandy, sheltered in the south (try Jarve) and hugged by pines. On this Regent trip, you’ll see it all. https://www.mediafax.ro/english/alert-in.text: Alert in Galați: Radar signal detected in the Târgu Bujor Area / Moldova: Drone arrived from the direction of Ukraine / Romanian Defence Ministry Provides details UPDATE: Romanian Defence Ministry on the drone incident in Galați – No debris or signs of impact found The Romanian Air Force IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter currently flying over the Târgu Bujor–Matca area in Galați County has so far identified no signs of impact and has found no debris or other elements indicating that an object may have fallen on Romanian territory, according to the Ministry of National Defence. According to MApN, the air alert issued on Monday morning ended at 8:52 a.m., and the two Romanian Air Force F-16 aircraft returned and landed at the 86th Air Base in Borcea. The incident was first reported on Monday morning, at around 6:00 a.m., when the Defence Ministry’s radar surveillance system detected intermittent signals in Moldovan airspace, in the Cahul area. One of the signals subsequently appeared in the Târgu Bujor area of Galați County. Authorities sent a RO-Alert emergency message to the population, while two F-16 fighter jets and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter were scrambled to monitor the situation. The military helicopter is continuing checks in the Târgu Bujor–Matca area in order to clarify the situation and determine whether there are any traces of an object that may have entered Romanian national airspace. So far, MApN says no debris, signs of impact or other elements indicating that an object fell on Romanian territory have been identified. UPDATE: Drone arrived from the direction of Ukraine The Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Moldova said its airspace monitoring systems detected an unidentified drone entering Moldova’s national airspace from the direction of Ukraine and crossing the state border. The drone entered Moldovan airspace at 5:55 a.m., flying from the direction of Vinogradovka , Odesa region, toward the city of Vulcănești, in Moldova’s Gagauz Autonomous Territorial Unit. At 6:09 a.m., it was recorded leaving Moldovan airspace from the direction of Pașcani, Cahul district, toward Romania, near the locality of Vlădești, Galați County. For this reason, Moldova temporarily restricted its national airspace in the southern part of the country for approximately 15 minutes, after which it was reopened. “The unauthorized overflight occurred following the Russian Federation’s air attacks on Ukraine during the night. National authorities, together with their partners, continue to monitor the airspace in order to ensure the safety of the population,” Moldova’s Ministry of Defence said. Initial report According to the cited source, one of the detected signals later appeared in the Târgu Bujor area of Galați County. To monitor the situation, two Romanian Air Force F-16 aircraft from the 86th Air Base in Borcea, as well as an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter, were scrambled. The National Military Command Centre notified Romania’s General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations (IGSU) that measures should be implemented to alert the population in the affected area. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/13/ukra.text: Menü Kereső A lengyel határ közelében csapódott teherautóba egy drón Ukrajnában, egy közeli vonat mozdonyát is találat érte Külföld Iván-Nagy Szilvia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Teherautóba csapódott egy drón az Ukrajnát ért orosz légitámadásban szombatról vasárnapra virradóra, alig 800 méterre a Dorohusk-Jahodin lengyel-ukrán határátkelőtől – közölte Dariusz Sienicki, a lengyel határőrség regionális alakulatának szóvivője. Az MTI híre szerint az Ukrajna nyugati része elleni orosz támadás miatt ideiglenesen leállították a forgalmat az összes lengyel-ukrán határátkelőn. A PAP lengyel hírügynökség szerint a legtöbb határátkelőn vasárnap délelőtt a közlekedés újraindult. Az ukrajnai helyzettel összefüggésben a lengyel kormány biztonsági központja vasárnap hajnalban sms-ben figyelmeztette a kelet-lengyelországi Lublini vajdaság és a délkelet-lengyelországi Kárpátaljai vajdaság több járásának lakosságát légitámadás lehetséges veszélyére, és emiatt riasztószirénákat is bekapcsoltak. Karolina Galecka, a lengyel belügyminisztérium szóvivője azzal indokolta az RCB által kiadott riasztásokat, hogy az orosz műveletek közel voltak a lengyel határhoz. Hozzátette azt is, hogy a lengyel oldalon nincsenek sebesültek. A nyugat-ukrajnai orosz légitámadások során rutinszerűen felszállnak a lengyel katonai vadászgépek, ez történt vasárnap hajnalban is, a művelet délelőtt véget ért – erősítette meg a lengyel fegyveres erők műveleti parancsnoksága. A járőrözés megelőző jellegű volt, a lengyel légtér biztosítását célozta, különösen a veszélyeztetett ukrán területekhez közeli régiókban. A lengyel légtér megsértését nem regisztrálták. A lengyel média az ukrán államvasutak közlését is idézi, mely szerint egy orosz drón eltalálta Ukrajnában a Kijev és Varsó között közlekedő személyszállító vonat mozdonyát akkor, amikor a szerelvény két kilométerre volt a lengyel határtól. A Gazeta Wyborcza cikke szerint a dróntámadásokat felügyelő társaság előre figyelmeztette a vonat személyzetét a fenyegetésre, aminek köszönhetően senki sem sérült meg. A lengyek PKP Intercity vasúttársaság közölte, hogy az utasok között nem voltak lengyel állampolgárok, még azelőtt történt a támadás, mielőtt a PKP Intercity átvette a vonatot. A vonaton 206 utas utazott. Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz lengyel védelmi miniszter ezt követően az X-en azt írta: a lengyel megfigyelőrendszerek tucatnyi Gerany-5 típusú sugárhajtású kamikazedrónt észleltek Ukrajna nyugati részében, ezek közül az egyik Lengyelország határától egy kilométeres, a másik pedig öt kilométeres távolságban csapódott le. A Kyiv Independent közben arról ír, az elmúlt nap orosz támadásaiban legalább hat civil halt meg és 43-an megsebesültek. Moszkva tömeges dróntámadásában ezúttal a távolabbi, nyugati régiók, így a fent említett lengyel határhoz közeli területek is érintettek voltak. Az ukrán légierő tájékoztatása szerint Oroszország 453 Shahed és Gerbera típusú drónt indított, ezek közül 405 drónt elfogtak. 13 helyszínen voltak becsapódások, és további hét helyszínről lehulló törmelékekről számoltak be. Ukrajna is támadást indított: két nagy orosz olajfinomítót vett célba a Krasznodari határterületen (Szavaszkij olajfinomító) és Tatárföldön (TANECO finomító). Mindkét célpontból tüzet jelentettek, továbbá az orosz hatóságok közlése szerint két ember meghalt és 12-en megsérültek a TANECO elleni támadásban. A TASZSZ orosz állami hírügynökség szerint a kórházba szállított sérültek közül ketten súlyosan megsérültek, egy ember középsúlyosan sérült, a többi sebesültet járóbeteg-ellátásban kezelik. A Krasznodari határterület operatív parancsnoksága szerint a lehulló dróntörmelékek megrongáltak egy gázvezetéket egy közeli lakóövezetben is. Photograph: Amir Levy/Getty Israel ‘Palestinians will bear the cost’: UK consulate in East Jerusalem prepares to shut its doors Forced closure marks low point in UK-Israeli relations, with reports UK is considering retaliatory expulsion of Israeli diplomats from London Israel marks three years since 7 October attack – live William Christou and Sufian Taha in Jerusalem Wed 7 Oct 2026 11.14 EDT First published on Wed 7 Oct 2026 10.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google T he UK consulate in East Jerusalem gave few signs it was at the centre of a geopolitical controversy this week, with little movement around the high-walled building save the fluttering of the union jack and the occasional car exiting the compound. The mission is to shut its doors on Thursday after Israel ordered its closure in response to a UK ban on trade with illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank and sanctions on those who help build or finance them. The forced closure marked the lowest point in UK-Israeli relations for decades, with reports of the UK considering a retaliatory expulsion of 27 Israeli diplomats from London. It would be the Palestinians who pay the price for the consulate’s closing, warned Amjad Iraqi, the International Crisis Group’s senior analyst on Israel and Palestine . The UK consulate in East Jerusalem is separate from the UK embassy in Tel Aviv – which remains open – and provides services to Palestinians in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza, services they will now lose. “It’s quite telling that the Israeli government response was primarily about blocking the UK’s ability to support Palestinians, rather than the core of UK-Israeli relations themselves,” Iraqi said. “For [the Israeli] foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, the response is low-cost, in their minds it’s just Palestinians bearing the cost.” UK threatens to expel Israeli diplomats over planned East Jerusalem consulate closure Read more Israel has already curtailed the diplomatic activities of the Netherlands, Spain and Norway in the occupied West Bank . Palestinian residents of Sheikh Jarrah, the East Jerusalem neighbourhood that is home to the consulate, appeared resigned when asked about the impact the closure might have on their lives. “I mean, it was the British that were the basis of the issue, wasn’t it? They were the ones who signed the Balfour declaration?” said Abu Abdo, a 79-year-old former repairman and resident of Sheikh Jarrah, referring to a 1917 document by the British foreign secretary Arthur Balfour, which expressed support for a Jewish state in Palestine. It was a dramatic end for the consulate’s tenure in East Jerusalem, which since its move to the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood in 1967 has experienced its fair share of political upheaval. The UK government first bought the plot that would become its consulate in 1963, when East Jerusalem was still under Jordanian control. It was meant to be a direct liaison between the UK government and the Jordanian-administered West Bank and East Jerusalem. The compound took four years to build and was finally ready for the UK consul-general to move into by 1967. By the time the new consul-general moved into the premises, however, East Jerusalem was no longer under the control of the Jordanians. Just weeks before John Henry Lewen was to move into the building, the six-day war broke out and Israel captured East Jerusalem from the Jordanian forces. Lewen assumed his post at the consulate in a changed East Jerusalem under Israeli control. The consulate he oversaw occupied a unique position as the UK did not recognise Jerusalem as being under any single country’s control. As the UK foreign secretary told parliament in June 1967: “Our consul-general in Jerusalem is subordinate neither to the ambassador in Tel Aviv nor to the ambassador in Amman, but directly to the Foreign Office.” Lewen’s tenure was marked by the political problems that plagued Jerusalem in the aftermath of the six-day war and the birth of Israel. In 1969, a bomb was placed under the window of a consul secretary, harming no one but damaging the compound. Years later, Palestinians would present their grievances to the British consulate in Sheikh Jarrah. In 2017, protesters demonstrated outside the consulate to mark the centenary of the Balfour declaration. Men placed flags in the consululate windows reading “Balfour is a crime”, while schoolgirls carried thousands of letters written by Palestinian students asking Britain to apologise for the declaration. This week, however, there was little sign of the political turmoil which the British consulate had waded through during its 60 years on the site. The neighbourhood, mostly made up of diplomatic missions and UN and other international organisations’ offices, was quiet. Residents in the area expressed disappointment over what they saw as a lack of international support for the Palestinian people in recent years. “We have seen very little but studies and words, no action from the international community,” said Abu Abdo. Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/Reuters View image in fullscreen Serhii Kuznetsov being escorted to a hearing in Karlsruhe, Germany, in November 2025. He was arrested in August that year while on holiday in Italy. Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/Reuters Nord Stream 1 pipeline Ukrainian soldier goes on trial over sabotage of Nord Stream gas pipelines Special forces officer Serhii Kuznetsov denies involvement in the 2022 blasts that left pipelines badly damaged Kate Connolly in Berlin Wed 14 Oct 2026 05.24 EDT First published on Wed 14 Oct 2026 02.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Ukrainian soldier has gone on trial in Hamburg accused of taking part in one of the most brazen acts of sabotage in postwar European history – the 2022 attack on the Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany . Serhii Kuznetsov, a special forces officer from the Ukrainian military, is accused by prosecutors of being an accomplice to war crimes by attacking civilian infrastructure, causing an explosion, damaging property and disrupting public services. Kuznetsov will be identified as Serhii K due to German privacy laws in the trial, which opened on Wednesday, but was referenced by his full name in an extradition order. He is alleged to have prepared and carried out the detonation of at least four incendiary devices of up to 27kg in weight at a depth of about 80 metres under the Baltic Sea, close to the Danish island of Bornholm. He is believed to have had six accomplices, including four deep-sea divers, an explosives expert and a ship’s captain, who are alleged to have used a rented yacht and timer-controlled explosives. Both he and his country deny any involvement in the attacks. The explosions took place on 26 September 2022, badly damaging the pipelines which had been constructed to carry Russian natural gas between Vyborg in western Russia and Lubmin, near Greifswald in northern Germany. View image in fullscreen Gas bubbles from the Nord Stream 2 leak reach the surface of the Baltic sea near Bornholm in October 2022. Photograph: Danish Defence Command/Reuters The blasts caused the Nord Stream 1 pipelines – Russia’s main gas supply route to Germany before Moscow cut the supplies in August 2022 – to burst. They also damaged Nord Stream 2, which was ready to carry gas but was never put into operation after Germany suspended its authorisation process just before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The attacks happened as European countries were seeking to transition away from Russian energy supplies in reaction to the Kremlin’s aggression. They exposed the dependence of Europe – and, in particular, Germany – on Russian gas as well as highlighting the murkiness of underground operations during wartime. Security observers initially blamed Moscow for the attack. Russia has denied involvement, in turn blaming the US , which has denied it just as forcefully . However, in July German state prosecutors accused Ukrainian “state authorities” of ordering the attack, arguing: “The aim was to permanently halt gas supplies via the pipelines and prevent Russia from using the revenue from natural gas trade to finance its war effort.” The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has denied his country was involved. Kuznetsov was arrested in August 2025 on a family holiday in Italy, with Italian police reporting that he surrendered without resistance. He had been travelling on a false passport. He was extradited to Germany last November, after legal efforts to prevent this failed. A further suspect, Volodymyr Zhuravlyov, an air conditioner installer and hobby diver, was arrested on a European warrant in northern Croatia in August. He is fighting his extradition to Germany having applied for asylum in Croatia. He denies any role in the sabotage. The Nord Stream riddle: echoes of mistrust ripple through Europe Read more Aware of how potentially incendiary the trial could be, with Ukraine effectively in the dock for a crime committed against its ally – and one of its staunchest wartime supporters – the German government has declined to comment on the proceedings. The far-right populist, pro-Kremlin Alternative für Deutschland party, which is soaring in the polls, has seized on the Nord Stream plot to boost its argument that German aid for Ukraine must cease and the pipeline be reinstated so that cheap supplies of gas can help counter the cost of living crisis. The trial is attracting much attention, not least because Nord Stream was already a highly controversial issue before the attack, involving Russia’s leader, Vladimir Putin, who, with the then German chancellor, Gerhard Schröder, managed to bypass Ukraine as a transit country with Nord Stream 1. After Schröder left the chancellery, Putin appointed him as chair of the supervisory board of the company Nord Stream AG. Schröder was seen last week attending Putin’s birthday celebration . View image in fullscreen Former German chancellor Gerhard Schröder, pictured at Vladimir Putin’s birthday party last week, was appointed chair of Nord Stream AG’s supervisory board by Putin after he left the chancellery. Photograph: Kremlin.ru/Reuters A request by the Russians to participate as co-plaintiffs in the Hamburg trial was rejected by the court. The company Gazprom, which owns the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, had argued its right to do so due to what it has referred to as the severe economic consequences resulting from the attack. The court argued that while repair costs of the pipelines would be high, it would not be economically impossible to restore them. According to reports, Kuznetsov, whose military ID indicates he was in active military service at the time the pipelines were blown up, is expected to maintain his right to remain silent during the trial. His legal team is expected to produce affidavits from two of his military superiors to support the argument that he is prohibited from revealing details of his actions as a soldier. He is reported to have allegedly taken his orders from a man who is considered to be the mastermind behind the attack and is one of those who has sworn in his favour. Sixteen trial dates have been scheduled at Hamburg’s Hanseatic higher regional court up to and including 17 December, with further hearings likely in January and February.
